model: Insurer FCFE at cost of equity, BVPS-compounding calibrated (engine route)

inputs.share_count_basis: 37.04M common shares on the Q3-2026 10-Q cover (2026-10-23) plus ~0.15M dilutive equity awards = 37.2M (down from 38.5M at the prior build; 3.4M shares bought back in 9M-2026 and ~0.36M more between 30 Sep and 23 Oct). Held FLAT going forward: SBC is expensed inside the pre-tax margin and buybacks are the use of the FCFE being valued, so shrinking the count as well would double-count the capital return. Roll-forward caveat: FY0 is still FY2025, so the model counts the whole of FY2026's FCFE while using a share count that already reflects ~$1.35B of FY2026 buybacks (and $233M of dividends already paid to earlier holders). That overlap (~$1.58B) is offset by the model discounting every flow as if the valuation date were still 1 Jan 2026 (10.5 months of accretion at 10% on ~$16B is ~$1.4B); the net overstatement is ~1% of value and is disclosed rather than bridged. It disappears when FY0 rolls to FY2026 at the 10-K.
inputs.debt_note: Everest carries $2,353M of senior notes, $218M of long-term subordinated notes due 2067 and $1,019M of FHLB borrowings (10-Q 2026-09-30). They are operating capital for a reinsurer and their interest ($107M in 9M-2026) is already deducted inside pre-tax income (the flow this model capitalises at the cost of equity), so net debt is held at ZERO in the bridge -- subtracting it again would deduct the debt twice. Recorded here for the reader; not an input to value.
inputs.fcf_basis_note: This is not a cash-flow-statement FCF. reported_fcf = FY2025 GAAP net income $1,591M + $61M SBC add-back (earnings before SBC); last_fcf = FY2025 net income $1,591M, the distributable-earnings (FCFE) base the model projects. Reported OCF ($3,068M FY2025) is float and reserve movement, not owner cash, and is deliberately not used.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash flow statement share-based compensation add-back ($61M, core_metrics stock_based_comp). Equity-award withholding taxes ($22M FY2025, kpis equity_award_taxes) are NOT added: for an insurer they are economically part of the buyback programme, not an unexpensed cost. Net investment income is the operating engine of a reinsurer, not surplus-cash interest, so interest_income is 0.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of EQUITY, not WACC: the flows are post-interest FCFE. USD build: 10-yr UST ~4.2-4.5% + reinsurer equity beta ~1.1 x ERP ~5.3% = ~10.0-10.3%, held at 10.0% (long rates rose in Q3-2026 -- the same move that cost $0.9B of AOCI -- but not by enough to re-base a through-cycle cost of equity; unchanged from the prior build). The 1.1 beta (vs a ~0.7 trailing market beta) reflects fundamental earnings volatility -- Everest's ROE has ranged 1% to 19% across the last decade on cat years and reserve charges -- and matches the ~10% cost of equity reinsurers and their rating agencies conventionally use. No further scenario or ratings-outlook premium is stacked on top; the reserve and pricing risks are carried in the bear scenario's margin path and its 25% weight, so risk is charged once. The SAME 10% applies to all three scenarios.
inputs.lease_treatment: Not applicable: operating leases are immaterial for a reinsurer (office space only) and are already expensed inside pre-tax income.
inputs.nci_treatment: Not applicable: no material non-controlling interests; Mt. Logan Re third-party capital is accounted for as reinsurance ceded / funds held, not NCI.
inputs.notes: MODEL (unchanged from the 2026-09-28 build): routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md row 'Insurer, holdco, compounder-of-book -> BVPS compounding x exit P/B'. Everest genuinely compounds book (BVPS ~$173 FY2015 -> ~$383 FY2025, 8.2% 10-yr CAGR, while paying $1.92->$8.00 DPS and halving the share count), so that row applies. To get validated dashboard sliders and the generated workbook the book-compounding logic is expressed on the FCFE-at-cost-of-equity engine route (same family as NAB.AX/IAG.AX): 'revenue' = total revenues (premiums earned + net investment income + realised gains + other); 'EBITDA margin' = pre-tax income before SBC as % of revenue (post-interest, post-cats, post-reserve development); D&A = 0; cash tax = 15% (Bermuda CIT; 9M-2026 GAAP rate 14.4%, FY2025 15.7%); 'capex' = RETAINED CAPITAL needed to hold equity/revenue at ~0.95x while premiums grow (retention = 0.95 x revenue growth); working capital = 0; net debt = 0. The terminal_cap_multiple is set per scenario so the exit lands on a price-to-book consistent with Everest's own history. THIS UPDATE (2026-11-19, Q3-2026 10-Q): anchors refreshed (price, equity, share count). Drivers re-judged: (1) FY2026 growth -7.5% -> -12.3% (9M revenue $11,742M, -10.2% YoY; Q3 -14.0%; premiums earned Q3 $3,156M, -18%); FY2026 margin 14.8% -> 14.3% (9M pre-tax $1,688M = 14.4% of revenue, with Q3 only $268M after $287M of Treaty cat losses and ~$293M more US casualty strengthening in Reinsurance Treaty; base Q4 pre-tax ~$450M allowing a further top-up at the year-end reserve review); FY2026 retention 1.5% -> 0% of revenue because 99% of 9M earnings was actually returned. (2) FY2027 growth -3% -> -6.5%: net written premium is running -21% YoY ($9.2B for 9M, ~$12.1B annualised) against ~$13.3B of FY2026 earned premium, so FY2027 earned premium of ~$12.0B is largely already written; with ~$2.4B NII that is ~$14.3B of revenue. (3) Normalised margin +0.5pt in base (13.0% -> 13.5%) and bull (15.0% -> 15.5%) from FY2027: the revenue base is ~9% lower than the prior build assumed while net investment income is higher ($634M in Q3, $1,725M for 9M, +10%), so NII is ~17% of revenue rather than ~14.5% -- a mix shift worth ~+2pt of pre-tax margin mechanically, of which only 0.5pt is taken because Q3 showed casualty strengthening spreading to the core Treaty segment outside the ADC. Bear margin path unchanged (the Q3 strengthening is direct evidence FOR it). SBC path rebased 0.35% -> 0.40% of the smaller revenue (FY2026 run-rate ~$62M). DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED: growth from FY2028, retention from FY2027, tax 15%, cost of equity 10%, terminal growth, terminal caps (12.5x/13.5x/10x), weights 25/50/25, 15% hurdle. See valuation_philosophy.unchanged_and_what_would_move_it. CALIBRATION CHECK after rebuild: base FY2026 net income ~$1.81B (9M actual $1.445B), FY2028 ~$1.63B = 11.4% on reported book of $14.25B and 10.5% on book ex the bond mark -- the 'about 11% ROE' anchor of the prior build is preserved; the implied through-cycle combined ratio is ~100% (the prior build's stated '~94% group CR' was not what a 13% margin implied -- on its own numbers it was ~98.6%; 2021-2025 actual average 97.1%, 9M-2026 96.3%). Exit P/B at year 10 on book rolled forward by retention: base 1.09x, bull 1.37x, bear ~0.60x. The bear exit was described as ~0.8x in the prior build; on this roll-forward it is ~0.6x under both the old and new drivers. The bear cap is left at 10x (a prior judgment, no new evidence on it) but the description is corrected. House and street bases differ only by the 0.4%-of-revenue SBC charge; the band is narrow, not collapsed.
inputs.buyback_cash_ytd_note: 9M-2026 buybacks $1,200M (3.4M shares, ~$353 average) and dividends $233M = $1,433M, 99% of 9M net income of $1,445M. buyback_cash above remains the FY2025 full-year figure ($797M) because FY0 is FY2025.
inputs.book_value_note: Equity $14,252M / 37.4M shares at 2026-09-30 = $381.1. Equity fell $1,178M in Q3 despite $233M of net income: $882M of other comprehensive loss (almost all unrealised depreciation on available-for-sale bonds as rates rose; AOCI is now -$1,314M, of which securities -$1,215M) plus $474M of buybacks and $75M of dividends. Excluding the securities mark, BVPS is $413.6. The mark is not an earnings event and pulls to par as the bonds mature; the model neither deducts it nor credits its recovery.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3-yr CAGR (22.4%) and EPS/net-income 3-yr CAGRs (35-39%) are measured off the FY2022 trough (Hurricane Ian, $1.6B AOCI bond mark-down that depressed equity to $8.4B) and include the May-2023 $1.5B equity raise; they are not sustainable rates. Revenue 5-yr CAGR of 12.8% reflects the 2021-2024 hard-market expansion that management is now deliberately reversing (FY2026 revenue shrinking). The per-share book-value CAGR (8.2% over 10 years, 9.6% over 5) is the only series that describes what a shareholder actually compounded, and is the selected rate. 'fcf' CAGRs are computed on GAAP net income (the distributable-earnings proxy for an insurer), not reported OCF.
historical_growth.notes: CAGRs are FY2025-based and unchanged from the prior build (no new fiscal year). BVPS approximated as period-end equity / weighted diluted shares for FY2015 (~$173) and FY2020 (~$243), and equity / cover-page shares for FY2025 (~$383). Year-end P/B history (FY2015-FY2025): 1.06, 1.12, 1.09, 1.13, 1.24, 0.97, 1.08, 1.54 (FY2022 AOCI-depressed book), 1.16, 1.12, 0.89; now 1.10x on $381 reported BVPS at 2026-09-30 and 1.02x on $414 ex the unrealised bond mark. SBC is 0.35-0.40% of revenue throughout, so the SBC-adjusted and reported earnings CAGRs do not diverge.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 -12.3%: 9M revenue $11,742M (-10.2% YoY) plus a Q4 of ~$3.6B (earned premium ~$3.05B on the Q3 trajectory, NII ~$0.6B). FY2027 -6.5%: net written premium is running at ~$12.1B annualised (-21% YoY) so ~$12.0B of FY2027 earned premium is largely already written; Legacy is now only ~$80M a quarter of GWP so the run-off drag is nearly complete, and core GWP (Treaty -5%, Wholesale & Specialty +3% in Q3) is roughly flat-to-down into softer property rates. FY2028 onward UNCHANGED: 2-3% nominal growth fading to 2.5%, now off a ~$14.3B trough rather than ~$15.7B.
base.margin_rationale: Pre-tax income + SBC as % of revenue. 9M-2026 actual 14.4% ex-SBC (combined ratio 96.3%: Q1 91.2, Q2 92.0, Q3 107.1); FY2025 11.2%; FY2024 9.0%. FY2026 14.3% = 9M actual + a Q4 of ~$450M pre-tax (a clean quarter is ~$650M; ~$200M is allowed for the year-end casualty review). FY2027 13.0% (soft property market) and 13.5% normalised, each +0.5pt on the prior build for the NII mix shift described in inputs.notes. 13.5% on ~$14.6B is ~$1.63B of net income = ~11.4% on reported book, ~10.5% ex the bond mark, and implies a through-cycle combined ratio of ~100% with NII ~$2.4B.
base.capex_rationale: Retained capital: equity/revenue held at ~0.95x, so retention = 0.95 x growth (1.9% at 2% growth, 2.85% at 3%, 2.4% at 2.5%). FY2026 set to 0%: 9M buybacks plus dividends were 99% of net income, so the prior build's assumption that ~25% of earnings would be retained under the negative rating outlooks did not happen. FY2027 left at 1.5% (UNCHANGED, deliberately conservative: equity is already ~1.0x FY2027 revenue and revenue is shrinking).
base.terminal_rationale: UNCHANGED. Gordon at 10%/2.5% = 13.7x FCFE; the 12.5x cap binds and pins the exit at ~1.09x book rolled forward by retention, the 10-yr median year-end P/B. Steady-state (ROE-g)/(CoE-g) = (11.4-2.5)/(10-2.5) = 1.19x corroborates with room.

bull.rationale: Q4-2026 reserve review is clean (FY2026 margin 15.6%, ~$2.0B net income); the Q3 Treaty casualty strengthening proves to be the last, core CR returns to ~90%, NII compounds on a $40B+ portfolio reinvesting at higher yields, and capital freed from retail insurance is redeployed into specialty/casualty reinsurance from FY2028. Growth FY2026 -12.0%, FY2027 -4.5% (re-judged with the base); FY2028+ unchanged. 15.5% margin (+0.5pt mix shift) = ~14% ROE; 13.5x cap (unchanged) pins exit at ~1.37x book, near the FY2019/FY2023 peaks.

bear.rationale: The Q3-2026 Treaty strengthening is the start of a third year of US casualty adverse development: a further ~$400-500M lands in Q4-2026 (FY2026 margin 12%, unchanged), a rating downgrade to A costs cedent share, and property-cat stays soft through 2028. Growth FY2026 -12.8%, FY2027 -9% (re-judged); FY2028+ unchanged. Margin path UNCHANGED at 9-10% (= ~8% ROE, below the cost of equity). The 10x cap (unchanged) puts the year-10 exit at ~0.6x book rolled forward by retention -- lower than the ~0.8x the prior build described, and well below the FY2025 year-end low of 0.89x; this is a harsh exit and is the first place to look if the bear looks too low.

scenario_narratives.base: Everest's reset is running deeper on volume than expected: 9M-2026 revenue is down 10% and net written premium down 21% as the AIG retail book runs off and property-cat capacity is cut, so revenue troughs around $14.3B in FY2027 (not ~$15.7B) before growing 2-3% a year. Q3-2026 was a poor quarter (107% combined ratio: $287M of Treaty cat losses and ~$293M of fresh US casualty strengthening in Reinsurance Treaty) after two clean ones; FY2026 still earns ~$1.8B because net investment income is running at ~$2.4B a year. From FY2028 a 13.5% pre-tax margin gives ~$1.6B of net income, about 11% on reported book, with underwriting roughly at break-even through the cycle and investment income doing the work. Essentially all of FY2026's earnings are being returned (9M buybacks $1.2B, dividends $233M); thereafter about a fifth is retained to support growth. Exit at ~1.1x book, Everest's 10-year median.
scenario_narratives.bull: The year-end 2026 reserve review is clean, the Q3 Treaty charge proves to be the last, and rating outlooks return to stable. Core underwriting runs at a ~90% combined ratio, NII keeps compounding as the portfolio reinvests at the higher yields that produced this year's bond mark-down, and from FY2028 capital freed from the retail book is redeployed into specialty and casualty reinsurance at 4-5% growth. Margins of 15.5% deliver ~14% ROE, well above the cost of equity, and the market re-rates the stock to ~1.35x book as it did in 2019 and 2023.
scenario_narratives.bear: Q3-2026's casualty strengthening in the core Treaty segment -- outside the $1.2B adverse development cover -- turns out to be the opening of a third year of reserve charges; another $400-500M lands in Q4, AM Best or S&P downgrade to A, and cedents trim Everest's share on large treaties. Property-cat pricing stays soft through 2028, so revenue shrinks to under $14B and stays there. A 10% pre-tax margin is an ~8% ROE, below the 10% cost of equity, and the stock is priced as a value-destroying compounder at a deep discount to book.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: UNCHANGED at 25/50/25 (house default 15/50/35). Bear stays at 25%: the Q3-2026 Treaty casualty strengthening (~$293M) is exactly the risk the elevated bear weight was set for -- it confirms the weight rather than raising it, because 9M prior-year development nets to only $226M after $141M of cat releases and the full-year verdict depends on the Q4 review. Negative outlooks from all three agencies remain. Bull stays at 25%: it still needs a clean reserve line, firm casualty/specialty pricing and a P/B re-rating together. What would move it: a Q4-2026 charge above ~$400M or any downgrade -> bear 30-35%; a clean Q4 review and outlooks restored to stable -> back toward 15/50/35.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Everest is a compounder of book value, so it is valued as one: the distributable-earnings stream (pre-tax income after interest, less tax and less the capital retained to support premium volume) is discounted at a 10% cost of equity with net debt held at zero, and the terminal value is capped so base and bull exit at a price-to-book consistent with Everest's own history (~1.1x / ~1.35x) and the bear at a deep discount (~0.6x). The question the model answers is whether a reinsurer earning ~11% on equity through the cycle and returning essentially all of its earnings deserves its current multiple of ~1.1x reported book (~1.0x excluding the unrealised bond mark). After the Q3-2026 refresh the answer is: about fairly priced on the weighted value, where at the prior build the stock sat at a clear discount -- the stock rose while the value edged down. Reported OCF, EBITDA and P/E are not used: for a reinsurer OCF is float movement, EBITDA is undefined, and a trailing P/E on years with ten-figure reserve charges says little.
key_risks_to_valuation: Reserve adequacy: Q3-2026 added ~$293M of US casualty strengthening in the core Reinsurance Treaty segment, outside the ADC. Every $500M of further adverse development is ~$13/share of book and, more importantly, evidence that the 13.5% normalised margin is too high -- the bear path, not a one-off.
Volume: net written premium is down 21% YoY. The model assumes revenue troughs at ~$14.3B in FY2027; each further 5% off the trough is roughly $20/share of base value at an unchanged margin.
Exit multiple: just under half of base-case value is the year-10 exit at ~1.09x book; at the FY2025 low of 0.89x the base IV falls by ~$35/share.

Catastrophe and geopolitical losses: 9M-2026 current-year cat losses were $556M (wildfire/weather $243M, earthquakes $157M, foreign conflict $146M); a 1-in-100 year has historically taken ROE to ~1-5%.

Rates: the Q3 rise in yields cost $0.9B of AOCI (BVPS $381 reported vs $414 ex the mark) but lifts reinvestment income; a 100bp fall in reinvestment yields is ~$300-400M of pre-tax income over time (~2.5pp of margin).

Roll-forward and share count: the model holds 37.2M shares flat, still counts all of FY2026's FCFE and discounts from 1 Jan 2026; the two effects net to a ~1% overstatement (see share_count_basis). It adds no value for repurchases made below intrinsic value.
unchanged_and_what_would_move_it: Growth FY2028-FY2035 (all scenarios): unchanged percentages off a lower trough. Moves on 1 Jan / 1 Jun 2027 renewal pricing and on whether core GWP (Treaty + Wholesale & Specialty) stabilises.
Bear margin path (12 / 9 / 9.5 / 10%): unchanged. Q4-2026 reserve review outcome moves year 1; a second Treaty charge in 2027 would argue for lowering the 10% normal.
Retention from FY2027 (0.95 x growth; 1.5% in FY2027): unchanged. A downgrade (retain more) or continued ~100% payout through 2027 (retain less) would move it.
Cash tax 15%: unchanged; 9M-2026 effective rate 14.4%. Moves if Bermuda amends the 2023 CIT Act's transition adjustment or Pillar Two treatment changes.
Cost of equity 10% and terminal growth 2.5/3/2%: unchanged. A sustained 10-yr UST above ~5% would re-base the cost of equity.

Terminal caps 12.5x / 13.5x / 10x: unchanged. Base and bull still land on 1.09x / 1.37x book. The bear's 10x lands on ~0.6x, harsher than the prior build described; raising it to ~12x (about 0.75x book, the steady-state value of an 8% ROE) would add ~$20 to the bear and ~$5 to the weighted value. Left for the owner of the model to decide.
Weights 25/50/25 and the 15% entry hurdle: unchanged (see weights_rationale).
